title: K-Means Clustering
explain: K-means splits points into K clusters by repeating two steps with K centroids: assign every point to its nearest centroid, then move each centroid to the mean of its points. Think of K magnets pulling points toward their centre of gravity. It stops when assignments no longer change, and it gives hard clusters. It is simple and fast but needs K up front and prefers round, similar-sized clusters. (K 个磁铁反复吸引样本, 并移动到各自重心.)
model:
It minimises **inertia**, the within-cluster sum of squares:
`J = sum_k sum_{x in C_k} |x - mu_k|^2`

```
seed K centroids (k-means++)
repeat:
    assign: each point -> nearest centroid
    update: each centroid -> mean of its points
    re-seed any empty cluster
until assignments stop changing (or max iterations)
```

Neither step can increase `J`, so it converges, but only to a **local** optimum. If an assignment pass changes nothing, the cluster memberships and therefore the means are the same: a fixed point.

**Choosing K:** inertia always falls as K grows (K = n gives 0), so look for the **elbow**, or the **silhouette** `s = (b - a) / max(a, b)` (a = mean distance to own cluster, b = to nearest other cluster), then ask what the product needs.

**Assumptions:** numeric features on comparable scales (standardize), roughly round clusters of similar size and density. Cost `O(n K d t)`.

Used to build the cells of IVF indexes ([similarity search](#/sd/f/similarity-search)) and to group [embeddings](#/sd/f/item-embedding).

details.q: Why does k-means converge, and to what?
details.a: The assignment step cannot increase inertia (each point moves to a closer centroid) and the update step cannot increase it either (the mean minimises squared error for fixed members). Inertia is bounded below, so it settles, but at a local optimum that depends on the seeds.

Use k-means++ (spread the initial centroids apart, choosing far points with higher probability) and run several restarts, keeping the lowest-inertia and stable result. Poor seeds give bad early partitions and high variance between runs. Re-seed any empty cluster with a new centroid.

Inertia always decreases with K, so the lowest value is meaningless. Inertia 1000, 400, 200, 180, 170, 165 for K = 1..6 has an elbow at K = 3: going 2 to 3 gains 200, 3 to 4 only 20. Confirm with silhouette and with what the clusters will be used for.

details.q: What does the silhouette tell you?
details.a: For a point, `s = (b - a) / max(a, b)`. With a = 2 and b = 6, s = 4/6 = 0.67. Near 1 means well matched to its own cluster, near 0 on the border, negative likely in the wrong cluster. Average it over points for a K.

details.q: Customers clustered on income (0 to 200,000) and age (18 to 80) come out as income bands. Why?
details.a: Euclidean distance is dominated by the larger-scale feature: a 10,000 income difference swamps a 30-year age difference. Standardize features (z-scores) first. Raising K does not fix the dominance.

Non-convex shapes (rings), clusters of very different density or size, and outliers that drag centroids. Consider DBSCAN, hierarchical clustering or a Gaussian mixture model. Features also need a meaningful Euclidean distance, so categorical data needs a different method.

details.q: Do one hand iteration to show you know the algorithm.
details.a: 1-D points 1, 2, 3, 10, 11, 12 with centroids 1 and 2. Assign: 1 goes to c1, the rest go to c2. Update: c1 = 1, c2 = (2+3+10+11+12)/5 = 7.6. Next pass: 1, 2, 3 go to c1 (mean 2), 10, 11, 12 to c2 (mean 11); then nothing changes and inertia is 4.

prompts.q: Explain k-means in under a minute.
points: K centroids, assign each point to the nearest one
Update each centroid to the mean of its points, repeat
Hard clustering, converges to a local optimum
Needs K, scaling and good seeds

prompts.q: How do you pick K and make the result trustworthy?
points: Inertia always falls with K, so use the elbow
Silhouette score as a second view
Tie K to the business purpose

prompts.q: Where does k-means appear in a retrieval system, and where does it break?
points: IVF index cells are k-means clusters of vectors
Query probes the nprobe nearest centroids
Outliers, uneven density and non-round shapes hurt it
Cells go stale as data drifts, so retrain
